title: Why We Don’t Need More Data Centers - Dr. Jasper Zhang, Hyperbolic

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk describes Hyperbolic as a GPU marketplace platform that other teams build on, matching the developer platform inclusion criteria. The platform serves software builders across multiple AI workload types, fitting both developer_platforms and general_purpose. The talk covers deployment and production infrastructure for GPU compute provisioning and model hosting. Requires basic understanding of GPU cloud computing, Kubernetes concepts, and AI workloads to follow the technical details. Conference presentation at AI Engineer World's Fair with slides, use cases, and Q&A. All key claims are directly stated in the transcript with supporting excerpts and evidence anchors.

summary: Dr. Jasper Zhang, CEO and co-founder of Hyperbolic, presents a case against endlessly building data centers to meet AI compute demand. He acknowledges data centers remain important but argues they alone cannot solve the problem. Demand projections show 22% annual growth, requiring 219 gigawatts by 2030 from the current 55 gigawatts. Challenges include billion-dollar construction costs (Stargate), seven-year grid connection waits in Northern Virginia, 4% of US electricity consumed by GPUs and data centers, and a projected 15+ gigawatt supply deficit even if all centers deliver on time. Meanwhile, GPU utilization is low—80% idle for enterprises—and the market is fragmented across 100+ GPU clouds. Zhang's solution is a GPU marketplace or aggregation layer. Hyperbolic built hyperdos (Hyperbolic Distributed Operating System), a Kubernetes agent that integrates any cluster into the network within five minutes. The architecture uses a feudal model: a monarch server coordinates with barons that own compute resources, provisioning machines and SSH access on demand. Users can rent via spot, on-demand, long-term reservation, or host models. The marketplace reduces costs 50-75% through queuing theory (M/M/C). H100 GPUs cost $0.99/hour on Hyperbolic versus $11 on Google and $2-3 on Lambda. A startup use case illustrates 6x savings: instead of reserving 1,000 GPUs for a year and adding 10,000 more for a month, companies dynamically scale and release idle GPUs, reducing costs from $43.8M to $6.9M. Zhang emphasizes this isn't just savings—with scaling laws, the same budget yields 6x productivity. He envisions the marketplace evolving into an all-in-one platform for online inference, offline inference, and training. He stresses sustainability benefits of reusing idle compute. Hyperbolic is launching business and enterprise clouds with 99.5% reliability.

sections.title: Introduction and Speaker Background
sections.summary: Jasper Zhang introduces himself as CEO and co-founder of Hyperbolic. He completed his math PhD at UC Berkeley in two years, won gold medals, and previously worked at Citadel Securities applying AI/ML to market prediction. He frames the talk around solving GPU compute costs, which represent a major expense for companies and startups requiring thousands of GPUs.

sections.title: The Problem: Data Center Demand and Challenges
sections.summary: Zhang presents demand projections: 22% annual growth requiring 219 gigawatts by 2030 from current 55 gigawatts. Challenges include billion-dollar construction costs, seven-year grid connection waits, 4% US electricity consumption, CO2 emissions, and a 15+ gigawatt supply deficit even if all centers deliver on time. He notes GPU utilization is low at 80% idle for enterprises, with 100+ fragmented GPU clouds.

sections.title: Solution: GPU Marketplace and Hyperdos
sections.summary: Zhang proposes a GPU marketplace or aggregation layer. Hyperbolic built hyperdos, a Kubernetes agent that integrates any cluster within five minutes. Users rent GPUs via spot, on-demand, long-term reservation, or model hosting. Benefits include solving compute matching, commoditizing GPUs, and offering multiple options. Cost savings of 50-75% are supported by M/M/C queuing theory. H100 costs $0.99/hour versus $11 on Google and $2-3 on Lambda.

sections.title: Use Case: Startup GPU Scaling and 6x Savings
sections.summary: A startup use case compares traditional cloud reservation versus Hyperbolic. Instead of reserving 1,000 GPUs for a year and adding 10,000 for a month, companies dynamically scale and release idle GPUs back to the marketplace. This reduces costs from $43.8M to $6.9M, a 6x saving. Zhang emphasizes that with scaling laws, the same budget yields 6x productivity, enabling startups to train models instead of relying on closed AI providers.

sections.title: Takeaways, Product Offerings, and Q&A
sections.summary: Zhang summarizes three takeaways: need smarter allocation not just more data centers, marketplace reduces costs, and reusing idle compute is more sustainable. He announces business and enterprise clouds with 99.5% reliability. In Q&A, he explains hyperdos is a Kubernetes agent using a feudal model: a monarch server receives user requests and dispatches to barons that provision machines and set up SSH access.
